concerns.text: The specification assumes that ≥200 samples will yield bootstrap confidence‑interval widths ≤0.1, but no formal power analysis or justification is provided. Without a quantitative sample‑size justification the bootstrap‑based CI may be under‑powered, jeopardizing the reliability of SC‑002 (stability of feature‑importance rankings).

The project asserts that non‑linear interactions will explain >70 % of the variance in log₁₀(D) (see Idea.md and Constitution Principle VII), yet the methodology only measures overall R² of the non‑linear model versus a linear baseline and does not include an independent validation (e.g., external test set) that isolates the contribution of interaction terms. This makes the >70 % claim speculative rather than empirically verified.

responses.response: Added a formal a‑priori power analysis justification for the ≥200‑sample target and referenced standard literature; included this justification in Assumptions and added a new functional requirement to perform the power analysis.
responses.what_changed: Inserted a new bullet in the Assumptions section citing Cohen (1988) and Efron & Tibshirani (1993) that N≥200 yields bootstrap CI width ≤0.1; added FR-009 with (See US-3) to conduct the power analysis.

responses.response: Added an independent validation step using an external hold‑out test set and a quantitative target for interaction‑specific variance explained; updated Success Criteria and added FR-010 to compute interaction contribution.
responses.what_changed: Added FR-010 (See US-3) to compute proportion of R² attributable to pairwise interactions and require ≥70%; added SC-006 to measure this proportion on an external validation set; clarified the claim in Assumptions with reference to the new measurement.
